title: Senate Floor Debate
subtitle: S.J.Res.185 — Directing Removal of U.S. Forces from Iran Hostilities

data.billTitle: A joint resolution directing the removal of United States Armed Forces from hostilities against the Islamic Republic of Iran

speakers.name: Sen. Tammy Duckworth
speakers.title: D-IL · Army Combat Veteran
speakers.quote: This resolution invokes the War Powers Act. No president — of either party — should wage war without congressional authorization. I served this country in uniform. I know what it costs. Congress must reclaim its constitutional authority.

speakers.name: Sen. Lisa Murkowski
speakers.title: R-AK · Senate Appropriations
speakers.quote: I support this resolution not because I oppose protecting American forces, but because the Constitution is clear: the power to declare war belongs to Congress. A vote here is a vote for that principle.

speakers.name: Sen. Tom Cotton
speakers.title: R-AR · Senate Armed Services
speakers.quote: Passing this resolution would signal weakness to our adversaries at a critical moment. Iran must understand that American resolve is absolute. We cannot afford to tie the Commander-in-Chief's hands while missiles are being launched at US assets.

data.title: What This Vote Means
data.text: S.J.Res.185 is a War Powers Resolution requiring the withdrawal of US Armed Forces from hostilities involving Iran within 30 days unless Congress explicitly authorizes continued action. The 50-47 vote passed the Senate, sending it to the House. The resolution has bipartisan support — 3 Republicans crossed party lines to vote with 47 Democrats.

data.title: Should Congress have the final say on military action against Iran?
